Recite the verses of "The Twelve Days of Christmas", each adding a gift to the one before.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/twelve-days) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: twelve_days.nomi
//# The lyrics of "The Twelve Days of Christmas".

once ordinals = Vector[
    "first",
    "second",
    "third",
    "fourth",
    "fifth",
    "sixth",
    "seventh",
    "eighth",
    "ninth",
    "tenth",
    "eleventh",
    "twelfth",
]

once first_gift = "a Partridge in a Pear Tree"

/// The gifts of the second day to the twelfth, in order.
once later_gifts = [
    "two Turtle Doves",
    "three French Hens",
    "four Calling Birds",
    "five Gold Rings",
    "six Geese-a-Laying",
    "seven Swans-a-Swimming",
    "eight Maids-a-Milking",
    "nine Ladies Dancing",
    "ten Lords-a-Leaping",
    "eleven Pipers Piping",
    "twelve Drummers Drumming",
]

/// The verses for days `start` to `end`, both included, counting from 1.
pub fn recite(start: Int, stop: Int) -> List<String>
    start..=stop
    |> Iter.map(verse)
    |> Iter.to_list()
end

fn verse(day: Int) -> String
    ordinal = Vector.get(ordinals, day - 1)!
    "On the ${ordinal} day of Christmas my true love gave to me: ${gifts(day)}."
end

/// Every gift given on `day`, newest first.
fn gifts(day: Int) -> String
    if day == 1 then return first_gift

    later =
        later_gifts
        |> Iter.take(day - 1)
        |> Iter.reverse()
        |> String.join(", ")

    "${later}, and ${first_gift}"
end

// FILE: twelve_days_test.nomi
import twelve_days

/// Each canonical verse on its own: its description, its number and its text.
once verses = [
    (
        "first day a partridge in a pear tree",

        "On the first day of Christmas my true love gave to me: a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",

        "second day two turtle doves",

    (

        3,
        "On the third day of Christmas my true love gave to me: three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",

        4,

    (
        "sixth day six geese-a-laying",
        6,
        "On the sixth day of Christmas my true love gave to me: six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
    (
        "seventh day seven swans-a-swimming",
        7,
        "On the seventh day of Christmas my true love gave to me: seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",

    (

        "On the eighth day of Christmas my true love gave to me: eight Maids-a-Milking, seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
    (
        "ninth day nine ladies dancing",
        9,
        "On the ninth day of Christmas my true love gave to me: nine Ladies Dancing, eight Maids-a-Milking, seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
    (
        "tenth day ten lords-a-leaping",
        10,
        "On the tenth day of Christmas my true love gave to me: ten Lords-a-Leaping, nine Ladies Dancing, eight Maids-a-Milking, seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
    (
        "eleventh day eleven pipers piping",
        11,
        "On the eleventh day of Christmas my true love gave to me: eleven Pipers Piping, ten Lords-a-Leaping, nine Ladies Dancing, eight Maids-a-Milking, seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
    (

        "On the twelfth day of Christmas my true love gave to me: twelve Drummers Drumming, eleven Pipers Piping, ten Lords-a-Leaping, nine Ladies Dancing, eight Maids-a-Milking, seven Swans-a-Swimming, six Geese-a-Laying, five Gold Rings, four Calling Birds, three French Hens, two Turtle Doves, and a Partridge in a Pear Tree.",
    ),
]

test "verse"
    subtests verses, (description, number, expected), description
        assert twelve_days.recite(number, number) == [expected]
    end
end

test "lyrics"
    [
        ("recites first three verses of the song",           1, 3),
        ("recites three verses from the middle of the song", 4, 6),
        ("recites the whole song",                           1, 12),
    ]
    |> subtests (description, start, stop), description
        expected =
            verses
            |> Iter.drop(start - 1)
            |> Iter.take(stop - start + 1)
            |> Iter.map(fn (_description, _number, verse) -> verse)
            |> Iter.to_list()

        assert twelve_days.recite(start, stop) == expected
    end
end
```

## How it's written

- The ordinals are a `Vector` read with `Vector.get(...)!`: the day comes from `recite`'s range, so an index out of bounds is a caller's bug, and a trap reports it (style §29).
- The first day's gift is a `once` of its own, apart from the later gifts, because it is the only one that changes: it gains "and" once another gift comes before it. `gifts` returns it alone on day one, and otherwise takes the later gifts, reverses them and joins them before ", and a Partridge in a Pear Tree".
- `String.join_list` with an English locale was the other way to write the "and", but CLDR's English list puts no comma before "and" in a list of two, and the song does.
- The test file holds each canonical verse once, in a `once verses` table. The single-verse cases are a `subtests` over it, and the three multi-verse cases take their expected verses from it with `Iter.drop` and `Iter.take`, since each canonical multi-verse case is exactly those verses in order. Writing the whole song out again for "recites the whole song" would add 40 lines of the same text.
